claims.statement: The three Spin(9)-covariant canonical EB orbit channels associated with v_H=(0,1,7,7), v_V=(1,4,4,6), and v_R=(1,0,0,14) admit exact finite projective-orbit POVMs with respectively 1152, 1008, and 144 rank-one effects. Their channels equal the continuous Spin(9)-orbit channels on the full matrix algebra M_16.
assumptions: The real 16-dimensional spinor Clifford model and its octonionic seed basis match the Cycle 9 conventions.
Even sign masks distinguish all Clifford subsets of grades 0 through 4, and PGL(2,8) is transitive on k-subsets for k=1,2,3,4.
The exact seed projective stabilizers and tight-frame checks in the finite compiler are correct.
claims.measurement_circuit_status: An exact Naimark isometry and a conservative generic gate-synthesis upper bound are given. The bounds are not optimized or practical; no efficient physical readout has been established.
claims.novelty_boundary: PGL(2,8) set-transitivity and group twirling are known. No novelty or priority claim is made for the finite Spin(9) realization.
claims.falsifier: A wrong Clifford character action, nontransitive subset layer, incorrect Spin lift, incorrect projective orbit/stabilizer, or failure of exact tight-frame identity invalidates the construction.

claims.statement: For any rational Spin(9)-covariant compatible-channel sector transfer vector lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_4) in the Cycle 9 theorem class, exact rational boundary enumeration returns q_H,q_V,q_R>=0 summing to one such that sum_i q_i eta_i,k >= 2 lambda_k-1 for every grade k. The corresponding pooled finite POVM is one full-domain canonical EB comparator.
assumptions: The Cycle 9 all-mixed Spin(9) star/support theorem guarantees feasibility for every legal compatible transfer vector.
Input transfers are supplied as exact rational values; floating-point inputs are rejected.
claims.falsifier: A legal compatible transfer vector for which the exact LP routine returns infeasible, or a returned q violating an exact grade inequality.

claims.statement: Every Spin(11)-covariant unital, trace-preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint channel on the complex 32-dimensional spinor with a CPTP two-output broadcaster having both marginals equal to the channel admits one full-domain canonical EB channel Psi with Psi >= 2 Phi - id on Hermitian matrices. Psi can be a convex mixture of four attained Spin(11)-orbit POVM channels.
assumptions: The standard Spin(11) spinor Clifford exterior-form identification End(S)=sum_{k=0}^5 Lambda^k R^11 and the stated triple-product decomposition are correct.
The exact ordinary-tensor star blocks cover all 32768 dimensions and both output-swap signs.
The exact mixed-weight PSD gaps and four attained seed moments in the certificate are correct.
The broadcaster Choi state has the stated TP and unital marginal constraints.
claims.external_proof_review: Parent assigned an independent Spin(11) audit; not claimed as completed by this package.
claims.full_canonical_EB_support: Not classified. The theorem uses support of an attained four-seed subset; a separate outer bound is not treated as equality.
claims.falsifier: A missing irreducible/swap block, incorrect seed moment, negative exact principal minor, normalization error, or legal broadcaster violating the four-seed dual support inequality.

verification.spin9_finite_compiler: Reran finite_compiler.py; exact group, lift, stabilizer, orbit, frame, seed moment, and rational mixture checks passed.
verification.spin11_extractor: Reran spin11_fullstar_blocks.py; full dimension and both swap-sector counts passed.
verification.spin11_seed_moments: Reran spin11_seed_moments.py; four moments matched exactly.
verification.spin11_mixed_support: Reran spin11_seed_support_check.py; 17 rays, 11 blocks, 629 exact principal minors passed.
verification.spin11_outer_support: Reran spin11_outer_support_check.py; 30 rays and 11 blocks passed. This outer bound is not used as exact canonical-EB support.

global_unknowns: The universal noncovariant/common-map factor-2 or dimension-free-c theorem remains open in this workstream.
No all-Spin(2n+1) theorem is established by the Spin(9) and Spin(11) finite checks.
The finite Spin(9) POVMs have exact finite definitions but no efficient physical readout circuit has been demonstrated.
